results.content:
The post from the official Google Research account recorded the highest spread in this list with 62,981 engagements. One of the biggest bottlenecks limiting LLM inference speed is the memory usage of the KV cache, and its reduction is a constant concern for researchers and developers. The fact that TurboQuant presented figures such as "6x reduction," "zero accuracy loss," and "up to 8x faster inference speed" strongly attracted the community's attention because it is accompanied by actual [...] Unresolved points include (1) the scope of free tier limitations and cost estimation when transitioning to production, (2) scale-up paths for Supabase/ChromaDB, and (3) the stability of self-hosted observability tools (Langfuse/Phoenix) in actual operation. At this point, the appropriate positioning is "it is confirmed to work on the free tier, but whether it is production-quality depends on each team's verification."

### Impact on Us [...] Skepticism/Criticism: "$0" is only at the PoC to prototyping stage, and production operations may face limitations from free tiers (Vercel's monthly bandwidth, Cloudflare Workers' execution time limits, ChromaDB's storage capacity). Furthermore, "free" is not "zero cost" and must be replaced with "self-hosting and learning costs." Engineering skills are essential for building Docker environments, implementing Ollama, and designing LangGraph.

### Fused decode+attend kernel (experimental)

The "speed flip" penalty above is almost entirely the dequantize step: at each decode token the compressed cache is expanded to fp16 before `scaled_dot_product_attention` runs, and at long context that materialization — not the attention math — is the wall. The fused kernel removes it. [...] | Flag | Meaning |

results.title: TurboQuant on Apple MacOS: Five Integration Paths  | Medium
results.content:
The counterposition: weights are the real bottleneck, not the KV cache. True for initial loading. But during running inference with long contexts (RAG, multi-turn, agents), the KV cache becomes the dominant memory consumer. On 24–48 GB systems, TurboQuant shifts this boundary measurably.

## Conclusion [...] ## Conclusion

TurboQuant is the missing piece for long-context local inference on Apple Silicon. The algorithm delivers. PPL 6.20 vs. 6.19 on Qwen3.5–35B-A3B. Over 70% KV cache savings on the full-attention layers. The integration landscape remains fragmented across five paths with different maturity levels. [...] oMLX includes TurboQuant KV cache as an experimental feature. Enable it in the Admin UI under Model Settings > Experimental Features. oMLX combines continuous batching and SSD caching on Apple Silicon. Paired with TurboQuant, it may be the shortest path to a near-production local inference server on macOS.

As of late March 2026, the TurboQuant toggle may be disabled pending a fix for the cache-merge prefill path. Verify current status before relying on this path.
